[[Doug LaMalfa]] | after_election = [[James Gallagher (California politician)|James Gallagher]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsCA}} The '''2026 California's 1st congressional district special election''' for {{ushr|CA|1}} in the [[United States House of Representatives]] was held on June 2, 2026, to fill the vacancy created by the death of incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. representative [[Doug LaMalfa]].{{cite web |last1=Ferris |first1=Sarah |title=California GOP Congressman Doug LaMalfa dies at 65 |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/01/06/politics/doug-lamalfa-congressman-california-dead |website=[[CNN]] |access-date=January 6, 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Gedeon |first1=Joseph |title=Doug LaMalfa, California Republican congressman, dies aged 65 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/06/doug-lamalfa-dies-california |website=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=January 6, 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Feinberg |first1=Andrew |title=California GOP Congressman Doug LaMalfa dies unexpectedly at age 65 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/doug-lamalfa-dead-california-rep-b2895449.html |website=[[The Independent]] |access-date=January 6, 2026}} A runoff between the top two candidates would have been held on August 4 if no candidate received a majority of the vote.{{Cite web |last=Chiochios |first=Nathan |date=January 16, 2026 |title=Gavin Newsom announces special election to fill Doug LaMalfa’s seat |url=https://www.chicoer.com/2026/01/16/gavin-newsom-announces-special-election-to-fill-doug-lamalfas-seat/ |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=The Press Democrat |language=en-US}} Although the election occurred after the passage of [[2025 California Proposition 50|Proposition 50]] in 2025, the proposition did not impact this election because the proposed map goes into effect for the term that begins on January 3, 2027, as the special election was for the term that expires on that date.{{Cite web |last=Graham |first=Andrew |date=January 6, 2026 |title=Gavin Newsom sets last possible date for special election to fill LaMalfa’s seat |url=https://www.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article314352965.html |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=[[The Sacramento Bee]]}} Republican state assemblyman [[James Gallagher (California politician)|James Gallagher]] won the election in this heavily red district by securing 62.10% of the total votes and defeating Democratic candidates Audrey Denney and [[Mike McGuire (politician)|Mike McGuire]] by a massive margin.{{cite news |title=Republican James Gallagher wins special election for vacant red House district in California |first=Ben |last=Kamisar |website=NBC News |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=June 2, 2026 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/republican-james-gallagher-wins-special-election-vacant-red-house-dist-rcna348179}} The special election also coincided with the primary election for the new district boundaries, in which Gallagher and McGuire both advanced, setting up a rematch in the November general election.{{cite news |title=Gallagher leads in two 1st District races for Congress, with McGuire staking claim to runoff |first=Austin |last=Murphy |work=The Press Democrat |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=June 2, 2026 |url=https://www.pressdemocrat.com/2026/06/02/gallagher-leads-in-two-1st-district-races-for-congress-with-mcguire-staking-claim-to-runoff/}} == Background == === Redistricting and scheduling === {{See also|2025 California Proposition 50}} In 2025, California voters passed Proposition 50, an amendment to [[Constitution of California|California's constitution]] that supplanted the map created by the [[California Citizens Redistricting Commission]] (CCRC) with a map that favors [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] candidates. As a result, District 1 was redrawn to be more Democratic-leaning, removing the Republican-leaning rural counties of [[Modoc County, California|Modoc]] and [[Siskiyou County, California|Siskiyou]] along with the [[Redding, California|Redding]] and [[Yuba–Sutter area|Yuba–Sutter]] metropolitan areas, while adding the Democratic-leaning city of [[Santa Rosa, California|Santa Rosa]].{{Cite web |last=Battaglia |first=Roman |last2=Grossi |first2=Sarina |date=2025-10-29 |title=From cattle country to wine country: How Prop 50 could reshape California's 1st District |url=https://www.ijpr.org/politics-government/2025-10-29/california-1st-district-map-change |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=Jefferson Public Radio |language=en}} In the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]], the newly redrawn 1st district would have voted for [[Kamala Harris]] by a margin of 54.5 to 42.3.{{Cite web |title=CA 2026 Congressional |url=https://davesredistricting.org/maps |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=Daves Redistricting |language=en}} [[Doug LaMalfa]] intended to seek reelection to the 1st district despite the new map before his death.{{Cite web |last=Arthur |first=Damon |date=2025-08-20 |title=Who's running for Congress in the district LaMalfa represents, so far |url=https://www.redding.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/08/20/whos-running-for-congress-in-the-district-lamalfa-represents-so-far/85732622007/ |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=Record Searchlight |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Hamann |first=Emily |title=California District Map Shakeup Puts GOP Seats in Jeopardy |url=https://pro.stateaffairs.com/ca/elections/california-congressional-map-shakeup |access-date=January 7, 2026 |website=State Affairs |language=en}} The congressional map drawn by Proposition 50 became official following the state's primary on June 2.{{Cite web |last=Holden |first=Lindsey |date=January 6, 2026 |title=A shocking death and a special election |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/california-playbook-pm/2026/01/06/lamalfa-death-california-00712997 |access-date=January 6, 2026 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}} As the primary for the special election was also held on June 2, the general special election used the current map drawn by the CCRC. A run-off for the general special election would have occurred on August 4 if no candidate received a majority of votes in the primary. Although most special elections use old district lines before a redistricting cycle, some previous elections have used newly drawn maps, including a special election for [[Nebraska's 1st congressional district|Nebraska's 1st district]] in [[2022 Nebraska's 1st congressional district special election|2022]].{{Cite web |last=Nir |first=David |last2=Singer |first2=Jeff |title=Morning Digest: Here's how Republican Rep. Doug LaMalfa's seat will be filled |url=https://www.the-downballot.com/p/morning-digest-heres-how-republican |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=The Downballot |language=en}} === Republican control of the House === LaMalfa died one day after the resignation of Republican [[Marjorie Taylor Greene]], bringing the total [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] in the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] to a bare majority of 218 to 213 [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] with four vacancies at the time.{{Cite web |last=Karni |first=Annie |date=2026-01-06 |title=LaMalfa's Death Further Depletes House G.O.P. Majority |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/06/us/politics/doug-lamalfa-house-republican-majority.html |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=The New York Times}} News organizations, including ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' and ''[[Politico]]'', noted that this narrow margin provided additional strain on the Republican majority and [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|Speaker]] [[Mike Johnson]], as the Republicans could only lose two votes, placing increased prominence on the special election.{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Meredith Lee |date=2026-01-06 |title=The House GOP confronts a shocking loss and a difficult road ahead |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/01/06/house-republicans-anxiety-margins-midterms-00713358 |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Beavers |first=Olivia |date=2026-01-06 |title=GOP Lawmaker's Death Pressures Republican Majority |url=https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/doug-lamalfa-california-dies-republican-house-majority-7789a167 |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |language=en-US}} ==Candidates==
